description: Project-specific documentation standards for master-model-maven (settled-decision stability, claim traceability, specification intent voice, coverage via BDD .feature evidence, MAOS spec codification, canonical AI-first structure). Checked by the pr-reviewer agent against documentation changes.

standards.title: Do not reopen settled design decisions without explicit instruction
standards.description: Design decisions recorded as settled (the Confirmed Design Decisions tables in CLAUDE.md, accepted ADRs, and decisional product-spec sections) are treated as fixed. A change must not silently re-litigate, contradict, or reverse a settled decision; doing so requires an explicit instruction or a superseding ADR referenced in the change.
standards.rationale: Settled decisions exist so they are not re-debated on every PR; a change that quietly reverses one reintroduces resolved questions and diverges code from documented intent. Source: CLAUDE.md (Confirmed Design Decisions); docs/adr/.
acceptance_criteria: No change in the diff contradicts or reverses a decision marked settled in CLAUDE.md, an accepted ADR, or a decisional spec section without citing an explicit instruction or superseding ADR.
A change that revisits a settled decision in the diff references the ADR (or instruction) that authorises the reversal.
Documentation edits in the diff do not delete or weaken a Confirmed Design Decision without a referenced authorisation.
anti_patterns: Re-introducing a separate consulting alert when single-delivery-per-submission is settled.
Editing a Confirmed Design Decision table to flip a decision with no ADR or instruction cited.
standards.source: Migrated from CLAUDE.md — Confirmed Design Decisions

standards.title: Every product-doc claim is traceable to a test or an open issue
standards.description: A claim of behaviour in a product/capability specification must either be specified as a scenario in a BDD .feature (generated from the capability) and realised by a passing executable test, or be accompanied by an open GitHub issue / roadmap gap that records it. New or changed behavioural claims are not left untraceable.
standards.rationale: Untraceable claims drift from the implementation and cannot be verified; tying each claim to a behaviour-spec scenario (with a test) or a tracked gap keeps the docs honest. Source: docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.1 (Claims are traceable); STD-PROC-008.
acceptance_criteria: Each new or changed behavioural claim in a specification in the diff has a corresponding BDD .feature scenario (realised by a passing test) or a referenced open issue/roadmap gap.
A documented behaviour added in the diff without a passing test links the gap that tracks the missing coverage.
The diff does not add a behavioural claim with neither a BDD/test nor a tracked gap.
anti_patterns: Documenting a new redirect/authorization behaviour with no BDD .feature/test and no open issue.
Adding a spec claim that contradicts the BDD/tests without updating either.
standards.source: Migrated from docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.1 — Claims are traceable

standards.title: Specifications state intent in future/invariant voice — no tests, no 'Planned/Future'
standards.description: Product and Capability Specifications (docs/product/) describe what the system must do in future/invariant voice — contracts, invariants, data model, authorisation rules, user-facing behaviour and outcomes. They do not reference test IDs/files or coverage/evidence state, contain no 'Planned' or 'Future work' headings, and do not track gaps (planned behaviour and gaps are the roadmap/issues, STD-PROC-005). When a specification disagrees with code, code wins and a type:debt/area:docs issue is filed rather than editing the spec in place.
standards.rationale: A specification that mixes intent with coverage, planned work, or test references stops being a trustworthy contract; keeping it pure intent lets a reader answer 'what does it do?' without inference. Source: docs/_process/02_product-led-design.md.
acceptance_criteria: Product/Capability specification changes in the diff are written in future/invariant voice ('Unauthenticated requests receive 401'), not 'we test that…'.
A specification in the diff contains no test IDs/file references, no coverage/evidence tables, and no 'Planned'/'Future work' headings.
A gap discovered in the diff is filed as an issue / reflected in the roadmap, not added as a markdown gap/TODO in the spec.
anti_patterns: A 'Planned' or 'Future work' heading in a product/capability specification.
A specification that cites a test file or says 'we test that X'.
A '❌ Status: gap' or 'what is NOT tested' section in a specification.

standards.title: Coverage is the BDD .feature's test evidence, not a hand-maintained doc
standards.description: Coverage — what is proven now — is the evidence status of the BDD specification: each BDD .feature scenario (generated from a capability) is either realised by a passing executable test (tests/features) or is an open gap tracked in the roadmap / a GitHub issue. Coverage is derived from the test evidence, not hand-maintained in a separate doc. A scenario with no passing test, or a failing one, signals an open gap (STD-PROC-005, STD-PROC-014).
standards.rationale: Deriving coverage from the .feature↔test evidence keeps it truthful and current; a hand-maintained coverage table drifts from reality and rots. Source: docs/_process/03 / 04; MAOS BDD Specification.
acceptance_criteria: Every BDD .feature scenario touched in the diff is either realised by a passing executable test or has a tracked gap.
Coverage in the diff is expressed via the .feature↔test evidence, not a hand-maintained coverage table.
A capability/behaviour added in the diff with no passing test links the gap (roadmap/issue, STD-PROC-014).
anti_patterns: Maintaining a separate coverage table that duplicates or drifts from the test evidence.
A BDD .feature scenario with no executable test and no tracked gap.
standards.source: Migrated from docs/_process/03 / 04; MAOS BDD Specification

standards.title: Follow the canonical AI-first repository structure and MAOS spec taxonomy
standards.description: The repo is a codified, AI-first product knowledge system. Specifications follow the MAOS taxonomy — five human- and machine-readable spec types: Product Specification (docs/product/product-spec.md — Purpose, Scope, Capabilities, Roadmap Alignment, Success Measures); Capability Specifications (docs/product/capabilities/<id>.{md|yaml} — Outcome, Business Context, Inputs, Outputs, User Journeys, Dependencies — STD-DOC-006); Roadmap Specification (docs/product/roadmap.yaml — Outcomes, Milestones, Dependencies, Risks, Measures; calculated — STD-PROC-014); BDD Specifications (Gherkin .feature under tests/features/{playwright,deno}/, referenced by capabilities); Decision Specifications (docs/product/decisions/<id>.md — rules, policies, operational decisions). Governing process narrative is docs/_process/; technical-architecture narrative is docs/_architecture/, which references the codified engineering standards in standards/ — the detailed policing layer that sits alongside the specs. Step definitions/fixtures under tests/; frontend in src/; edge functions and migrations in supabase/. Names are kebab-case; there is no docs/agile/ or docs/reviews/.
standards.rationale: One home per spec type, on the MAOS taxonomy, keeps the linear, backward-traceable knowledge chain navigable by humans and AI; the standards police engineering quality alongside it. Source: MAOS Specification Framework; docs/_process/.
acceptance_criteria: Specifications in the diff use the MAOS taxonomy (Product, Capability, Roadmap, BDD, Decision) and are both human- and machine-readable.
Product definition in the diff lives in docs/product/ (product-spec.md, capabilities/, decisions/, roadmap.yaml); behaviour specs are .feature under tests/features/.
Engineering policing rules in the diff live in standards/*.json (referenced by docs/_architecture/); process narrative in docs/_process/.
Names are kebab-case; the diff does not add docs/agile/ or docs/reviews/.
anti_patterns: A capability described only in prose with no Capability Specification artifact (STD-DOC-006).
Putting engineering policing rules in product specs, or product intent in standards/.
A camelCase id, or a hand-maintained roadmap status.
standards.source: Migrated from MAOS Specification Framework + docs/_process/ (AI-first product engineering)

standards.title: Specifications are codified to the MAOS templates (capability, product, decision)
standards.description: MAOS specifications are codified to a consistent, machine-readable template so humans and AI parse them identically. A Capability Specification has a stable kebab-case id and covers Outcome, Business Context, Inputs, Outputs, User Journeys, and Dependencies, and references its BDD .feature(s) — the capability is the canonical unit bridging product, roadmap, and verification (STD-PROC-013). A Product Specification covers Purpose, Scope, Capabilities, Roadmap Alignment, and Success Measures. A Decision Specification covers the rule/policy/operational decision, its context, and its consequences. Capabilities are named in business language, not implementation terms, and every spec links to its adjacent artifacts (module/outcome/BDD/evidence) by id.
standards.rationale: Consistent codified specs let AI generate capabilities, BDD, tests, and reports from them and let humans review them; freeform specs cannot be reasoned over or traversed. Source: MAOS Specification Framework (templates); docs/_process/02_product-led-design.md.
acceptance_criteria: A Capability Specification in the diff has a stable kebab-case id, the MAOS sections (Outcome, Business Context, Inputs, Outputs, User Journeys, Dependencies), and references its BDD .feature(s).
Capabilities in the diff are named in business language (e.g. 'Search Public Trees'), not implementation terms (e.g. 'Build Search API').
Product and Decision specifications in the diff follow their MAOS templates and link to adjacent artifacts by id.
anti_patterns: A capability named for its implementation ('Create React Component', 'Add Database Table').
A spec with no stable id or links, that AI/tools cannot traverse.
standards.source: Migrated from MAOS Specification Framework; docs/_process/02_product-led-design.md
